prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Same total. Different neutrophils.' Two equal wooden counting frames, each holding EXACTLY TEN solid round counters in two horizontal rows of five. Left frame: top row FIVE teal counters; bottom row THREE teal then TWO amber counters. Label above '10 total', below '8 neutrophils'. Right frame: top row ONE teal then FOUR amber; bottom row FIVE amber. Label above '10 total', below '1 neutrophil'. At bottom a simple key: one teal circle 'Neutrophil', one amber circle 'Other white cell'. Short note 'Look at the differential'. Tiny qualifier 'Illustrative tokens, not clinical thresholds'. Do not make these realistic cells: use flat wooden counters with no nuclei. The exact counts and colours are essential.

clinicalSources.title: St. Jude: Absolute neutrophil count and neutropenia

teaching.question: Why can a total white-cell count conceal a low neutrophil count?
teaching.answer: It sums all white-cell types. The differential reveals how many are neutrophils, so the same total can contain very different absolute neutrophil counts.

title: The differential changes the count
caption: The total white-cell count alone does not specify the absolute neutrophil count. These equal-size token groups have different neutrophil fractions.
alt: Two groups each contain ten tokens: one group has eight teal neutrophil tokens and two amber other white-cell tokens, the other one teal and nine amber.

review.notes: Counted left grid: five teal above, three teal plus two amber below, total ten and eight neutrophils. Counted right grid: one teal/four amber above, five amber below, total ten and one neutrophil. Legend colours match; qualifier explicitly excludes clinical thresholds. No invented cellular morphology.
